He currently serves as the head coach of the boys' basketball team at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle. Roy played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His nickname was "'''B-Roy'''", but he was also referred to as "'''the Natural'''" by Trail Blazers announcer [[Brian Wheeler]].{{cite web |title=Brandon Roy |url=http://www.broy7.com/roy/about |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090117114350/http://www.broy7.com/roy/about |archive-date=January 17, 2009 |access-date=December 3, 2008}}{{cite web |title=Broadcaster of the Week: Brian Wheeler, Trail Blazers |url=http://www.nba.com/features/wheeler_070209.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090503174922/http://www.nba.com/features/wheeler_070209.html |archive-date=May 3, 2009 |access-date=May 14, 2009 |work=[[NBA.com]]}} Roy was selected sixth in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the Trail Blazers, having completed four years playing for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. He became known for his immediate impact on the Trail Blazers.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/awards2007_rookie.html |title=NBA.com – Trail Blazers' Brandon Roy |work=NBA.com |access-date=November 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116115620/http://www.nba.com/news/awards2007_rookie.html |archive-date=January 16, 2012 |url-status=dead }} Roy won the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] in a near-unanimous vote in 2007. He was named to two [[All-NBA team]]s and as a reserve to the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game|2008]],{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2008/reserves_080131.html |title=Two Hometown Hornets Named as Reserves for 2008 NBA All-Star Game |publisher=NBA |access-date=May 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100321213749/http://www.nba.com/allstar2008/reserves_080131.html 2012 |access-date=July 1, 2012 |work=USA Today}} ==Early years== Born in [[Seattle, Washington]], Roy attended an African-American Academy elementary school.[http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2008/04/feb_17_an_allstar_roys_game_do.html "Roy's game does his talking"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926001321/http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2008/04/feb_17_an_allstar_roys_game_do.html |date=September 26, 2012 }}, by Seth Prince, ''[[The Oregonian]]'', April 15, 2008. He first started taking basketball seriously while playing for the [[Amateur Athletic Union]], one of the largest sports organizations in the United States.{{cite news |title=The Real Roy |first=Brian |last=Hendrickson |work=The Columbian |date=December 9, 2007 |url=http://www.columbian.com/sports/localNews/2007/12/12092007_The-Real-Roy.cfm |access-date=March 10, 2008 School (Seattle, Washington)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle, and was considered one of the state's best high school players.{{cite web|url=http://gohuskies.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/roy_brandon00.html |title=Player Bio: Brandon Roy |access-date=November 12, 2008 |url-status=dead [[2002 NBA draft]] straight out of high school, but he withdrew his name after consideration.{{cite web |title=Brandon Roy |publisher=InsideHoops.com |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/players/brandon-roy.shtml |access-date=May 15, 2007 |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930181424/http://www.insidehoops.com/players/brandon-roy.shtml |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Brandon_Roy_timeline-255595-1218.html |title=BLAZERS: Brandon Roy timeline |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 12, 2008 |archive-date=December 23, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081223003235/http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Brandon_Roy_timeline-255595-1218.html |url-status=live }} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Scout.com]], Roy was listed as the No. 6 shooting guard and the No. 36 player in the nation in 2002.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/10589n-brandon-roy Brandon Roy Recruiting Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20150125074952/http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/10589n-brandon-roy |date=January 25, 2015}} ==College career== Roy faced challenges before entering college. His parents and his older brother had not attended college, and due to a learning disability, Roy had difficulty with the [[SAT]]; his reading comprehension was slow, which increased the time he needed for tests. He had taken the test four times (with tutors) before finally meeting the [[NCAA]] requirements. Unsure whether he would be able to attend a four-year college, Roy worked on the Seattle docks, cleaning [[shipping container]]s for $11 per hour. In 2002, Roy started to play for the [[University of Washington]] (UW). He remained there for four years under head coach [[Lorenzo Romar]]. He majored in [[Ethnic studies|American Ethnic Studies]].{{cite web |title=Prospect Profile – Brandon Roy |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/BrandonRoy.html |access-date=May 15, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070705071519/http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/BrandonRoy.html |archive-date=July 5, 2007 |url-status=dead }} After his junior year, Roy considered entering the [[2005 NBA draft|draft]], but changed his mind when he learned that teammate [[Nate Robinson]] and high school senior and UW signee [[Martell Webster]] intended to enter the draft. He saw an opportunity to rise in the ranks on his college team, and improve his draft position. On December 29, 2005, Roy led the Huskies to victory over the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]] with a college career-high 35 points and became the 31st Washington player to score 1,000 points in a career.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253630264|title=Roy scores career-high 35 in Huskies' Pac-10 opener|date=December 29, 2005|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 29, 2005|archive-date=November 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131108170322/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253630264|url-status=dead}} The following game he equalled his career high of 35 points in a double overtime loss to the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253650264|title=No. 7 UW upset, nation's longest home streak ends|date=December 31, 2005|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 31, 2005|archive-date=November 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131108170320/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253650264|url-status=dead}} During his senior year, Roy averaged 20.2 points per game while leading the Huskies to a 26–7 season and a second straight [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet Sixteen]] appearance.{{cite web|title=UW Huskies Have Sweet 16 Matchup With UConn Huskies |url=http://gohuskies.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032106aaa.html |access-date=May 15, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081223065630/http://gohuskies.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032106aaa.html |archive-date=December 23, 2008 }} Roy was named [[Pac-10]] player of the year and received [[All-America]]n honors at the end of the season, while also being a finalist for the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden]], [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]], [[Oscar Robertson Trophy|Oscar Robertson]], and [[Adolph Rupp Trophy|Adolph Rupp]] awards. Roy had a 2006 pre-draft workout with the Trail Blazers prior to being selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves as the sixth overall pick. However, he was immediately traded to the Trail Blazers for the draft rights of [[Randy Foye]].{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Land Brandon Roy and LaMarcus Aldridge |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Trail_Blazers_Land_Brandon_Roy-183312-1177.html |access-date=May 15, 2007 |archive-date=December 28, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071228041019/http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Trail_Blazers_Land_Brandon_Roy-183312-1177.html |url-status=live}} On January 22, 2009, before a University of Washington Huskies home game versus the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]], his number 3 uniform was retired.{{cite web|title=Roy's number to be retired tomorrow at game against USC |url=http://dailyuw.com/2009/1/21/roys-number-be-retired-tomorrow-game-against-usc |access-date=January 21, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100204045706/http://dailyuw.com/2009/1/21/roys-number-be-retired-tomorrow-game-against-usc |archive-date=February 4, 2010}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2006–2011)=== ====2006–07 season: Rookie of the Year==== [[File:Brandon Roy.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|Roy during the [[2006 NBA draft]]]] Roy's NBA debut was in his hometown against the [[Seattle SuperSonics]].{{cite news |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/sports/2003298624_kelley11.html |title=Roy is just the player to help the Blazers make a turnaround |last=Kelly |first=Steve |access-date=November 12, 2008 |work=The Seattle Times |date=October 11, 2006 |archive-date=December 29, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081229235956/http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/sports/2003298624_kelley11.html?syndication=rss |url-status=live }} He scored 20 points in that game and 19 in the following game.{{cite news|title=Roy receives 127 of 128 first-place votes as top rookie|agency=Associated Press|work=espn.com|date=May 2, 2007|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=2857872|access-date=February 4, 2020|archive-date=January 31, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131012053/https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=2857872|url-status=live}} An impingement in his left heel kept him out of 20 games early in the season, but he scored his first career [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]] shortly after his return, on December 22, 2006, against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. At the end of January 2007, Roy led all NBA rookies with 14.5 points per game. He became the fourth Trail Blazer to be selected for the rookie squad of the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] [[NBA All-Star Weekend Rookie Challenge|Rookie Challenge]] since its inception in 1994. He was the first Trail Blazer to participate in the All-Star Weekend since [[Rasheed Wallace]]'s selection as an [[2001 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star reserve in 2001]].{{cite news|title=Guard Brandon Roy makes rookie-sophomore game at All-Star event|agency=Associated Press|work=espn.com|date=January 31, 2007|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2749638|access-date=March 7, 2008|archive-date=November 6, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106071053/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2749638|url-status=live}} He was the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]]'s Rookie of the Month in January, February, and March 2007. After averaging 16.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game during the [[2006–07 NBA season]], Roy was named [[NBA Rookie of the Year]]. He received 127 out of 128 first-place votes. Due to injury, he played in only 57 games in that season, the second-fewest games for a Rookie of the Year. He was the third Trail Blazer to win the award, the first two being [[Geoff Petrie]] and [[Sidney Wicks]]. ====2007–08 season: First All-Star selection==== Roy started in the first 48 games of the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], averaging 19.1 points, 5.8 assists and 4.6 rebounds. He also led the Blazers to a 13-game winning streak in the month of December. Roy was selected as a reserve for the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game]]. He scored 18 points in that game, and also had 9 rebounds. He injured his right ankle in the final game before the All-Star Weekend. Although he earned accolades for his play over the weekend, the injury impacted his play in the following weeks.{{cite news|title=Roy could miss L.A. trip|first=Joe|last=Freeman|date=February 25, 2008|work=The Oregonian}} He played in the Rookie Challenge for the second time, this time as a "sophomore"; teammate [[LaMarcus Aldridge]] was also on the sophomore squad.{{cite news|title=Roy crashes a party|first=Geoffrey C.|last=Arnold|date=February 16, 2008|work=The Oregonian}} Roy played about 29 minutes in the All-Star game, the most of any Western Conference player. He also tied [[Chris Paul]] and [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] for the most points with 18.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20080217/ESTWST/boxscore.html|title=2008 NBA All-Star Boxscore|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 17, 2008|access-date=March 7, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080225131926/http://www.nba.com/games/20080217/ESTWST/boxscore.html|archive-date=February 25, 2008|url-status=dead}} ====2008–09 season: First All-NBA selection==== [[File:Brandon Roy Wizards.jpg|thumb|left|Roy handles the ball during a 2008 game]] In the 2008 preseason, Roy underwent a 20-minute medical procedure in [[Vancouver, Washington]], during which team physician Don Roberts removed a piece of [[cartilage]] that was causing irritation in Roy's left knee. Roy missed several weeks of action because of the rehabilitation, but was ready on the opening day of the season against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://myespn.go.com/blogs/truehoop/0-33-179/Report--Brandon-Roy-Will-Be-Ready-for-Opening-Day.html |title=Report: Brandon Roy Will Be Ready for Opening Day |date=August 14, 2008 |access-date=August 15, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820101844/http://myespn.go.com/blogs/truehoop/0-33-179/Report--Brandon-Roy-Will-Be-Ready-for-Opening-Day.html |archive-date=August 20, 2008 }} On November 6, against the Houston Rockets, Roy hit a game-winning 30-foot jumper in overtime with eight tenths of a second left.{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/story/?id=255047 |title=Roy's Buzzer-Beater Lifts Blazers Past Yao, Rockets in OT |access-date=November 9, 2008 |archive-date=December 23, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081223001105/http://www.tsn.ca/nba/story/?id=255047 |url-status=live}} On December 18, Roy scored a career-high 52 points against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He made 14 of 27 shots from the field, 19 of 21 from the free-throw line, and 5 of 7 from the three-point line. He also added six assists, five rebounds and a blocked shot, all without a turnover.{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281218022 |title=Blazers end 11-game skid vs. Phoenix behind Roy's career-high 52 |publisher=ESPN |date=December 18, 2008 |access-date=December 20, 2008 |archive-date=December 20, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081220195708/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281218022 |url-status=dead }} On January 24, Roy tied a [[Portland Trail Blazers|Blazers]] franchise record with 10 steals against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290124022 |title=Roy swipes 10 steals, Oden continues encouraging play in Blazers' win |publisher=ESPN |date=January 24, 2009 |access-date=January 25, 2009 |archive-date=February 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090201053302/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290124022 |url-status=dead }} On February 8 with the Blazers trailing by 1 against the [[New York Knicks|Knicks]], Roy made a layup at the buzzer to win it 109–108.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20090208/NYKPOR/recap.html |title=Roy's layup at buzzer gives Blazers win vs. Knicks |work=NBA.com |date=February 8, 2009 |access-date=February 8, 2009 |archive-date=February 12, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212063718/http://www.nba.com/games/20090208/NYKPOR/recap.html |url-status=live }} As of February 16, 2009, Roy has had 24 shots which tied or won the games with 35 seconds or less. Roy was again selected as a reserve in the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game]], where he scored 14 points in 7-for-8 shooting, grabbed 5 boards, and dished out 5 assists in a game-high 31 minutes of action. On April 13, Roy was named Western Conference Player of the Week for his fourth time. At the time, [[Clyde Drexler]] was the only other Portland Trail Blazers to have won the award four times.{{cite web |url=http://www.blazersedge.com/2009/4/13/833981/brandon-roy-is-pretty-good |title=Brandon Roy Is Pretty Good |date=April 13, 2009 |access-date=April 13, 2009 |archive-date=January 31, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131012057/https://www.blazersedge.com/2009/4/13/833981/brandon-roy-is-pretty-good |url-status=live }} Roy finished 9th in MVP voting for the 2008–09 season, garnering one 4th-place vote and four 5th-place votes for a total of 7 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/05/04/mvp.release.20090504/index.html |title=NBA.com: James outdistances Bryant in winning Kia MVP award |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=May 4, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090507190209/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/05/04/mvp.release.20090504/index.html |archive-date=May 7, 2009 }} Roy was named to the [[All-NBA Second Team]] on May 13, and was the first Blazer to make an All-NBA team since the 1991–92 season.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Brandon_Roy_Name_To_AllNBA_Se-312795-1218.html |title=Brandon Roy Earns All-NBA Second Team Honors |work=Portland Trail Blazers |publisher=NBA |access-date=May 17, 2010 |archive-date=March 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100321120421/http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Brandon_Roy_Name_To_AllNBA_Se-312795-1218.html |url-status=live }} ====2009–10 season: Second All-NBA selection==== [[File:Brandon Roy vs wizards.jpg|thumb|Roy defending [[DeShawn Stevenson]] in a game]] On August 5, 2009, it was confirmed that Roy had agreed to a four-year [[NBA Salary Cap#Individual contracts under the CBA|maximum-salary contract]] with a fifth-year player option, keeping him a Trail Blazer until at least the 2013–14 season.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4379864 |title=Roy agrees to extension with Blazers |publisher=ESPN |date=August 6, 2009 |access-date=September 13, 2009 |archive-date=August 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090811000746/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=4379864 |url-status=live}} Roy was selected to compete in the [[2010 NBA All-Star Game]], marking his third selection as an NBA All-Star. However, Roy was sidelined because of a right hamstring injury he sustained on January 13 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], and re-aggravated on January 20 against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On April 11, 2010, Roy injured his right knee. [[Magnetic resonance imaging]] that night confirmed a right knee bone contusion (bone bruise) and on April 12, further examination of the MRI showed a slight meniscus tear. Roy underwent surgery on April 16 and was expected to miss at least the first round of the [[2010 NBA playoffs]], but returned for Game 4 after eight days of recovery time to lead the Blazers to a win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2010/news/story?id=5095872|agency=Associated Press|title=Roy to miss postseason|work=ESPN.com|date=April 16, 2010|access-date=February 4, 2020|archive-date=December 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222103635/https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2010/news/story?id=5095872|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/TrueHoop/post/_/id/15382|author=John Hollinger|title=Roy returns for Trail Blazers|work=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2010|access-date=February 4, 2020|archive-date=February 4, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204065919/https://www.espn.com/blog/TrueHoop/post/_/id/15382|url-status=live}} Roy was named to the All-NBA Third Team on May 6, and this was his second season in a row to be named to an All-NBA Team.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/06/all.nba |title=Best on offense (Durant), defense (Howard) pace All-NBA team |publisher=NBA |access-date=May 17, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513011712/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/06/all.nba |archive-date=May 13, 2010 }} Shortly before the next season began, conference rival [[Kobe Bryant]] called Roy the hardest player to guard in the Western Conference, claiming he had "no weaknesses in his game."{{cite web |last=Nelson |first=Ryne |url=http://www.slamonline.com/nba/kobe-bryant-roy-over-durant/#GbXwya45mTbO0VRZ.97 |title=Kobe Bryant: Roy over Durant |publisher=SLAM |date=October 23, 2010 |access-date=April 15, 2017 |archive-date=April 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170416234447/http://www.slamonline.com/nba/kobe-bryant-roy-over-durant/#GbXwya45mTbO0VRZ.97 |url-status=live}} Roy was the cover athlete for [[NBA 10: The Inside]].{{Cite web |author=I. G. N. Staff |date=2009-09-14 |title=Portland Trail Blazers All-Star Brandon Roy Scores Cover of NBA 10: The Inside For the PSP |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2009/09/14/portland-trail-blazers-all-star-brandon-roy-scores-cover-of-nba-10-the-inside-for-the-psp |access-date=2022-10-22 |website=IGN |language=en}} ====2010–11 season: Final season in Portland==== Roy started the first month of the season scoring at his normal rate, but by December it started showing that his knees, which have bothered him since college and were injured in April, were ailing due to lack of cartilage. He missed nine games before the Trail Blazers announced that he would be out indefinitely.{{cite web|url=http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2010/12/30/Brandon-Roy-out-indefinitely/UPI-21061293762954/|author=UPI.com|title=Brandon Roy out indefinitely|publisher=UPI.com|access-date=October 23, 2011|archive-date=November 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105225209/http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2010/12/30/Brandon-Roy-out-indefinitely/UPI-21061293762954/|url-status=live}} [[File:Trail Blazers starting five fall 2009.jpg|thumb|left|Roy with his Portland teammates]] On January 17, 2011, Roy underwent arthroscopic surgery on both of his knees.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6031896|title=Brandon Roy has surgery on both knees|date=January 18, 2011|agency=Associated Press|access-date=October 23, 2011|archive-date=January 21, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110121201440/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=6031896|url-status=live}} He returned to the lineup on February 25, scoring 18 points off the bench, including a clutch three-pointer to force overtime, and helping the Blazers defeat the [[Denver Nuggets]] 107–106.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-02-26-blazers-nuggets_N.htm|agency=Associated Press|title=Blazers beat 'Melo-less Nuggets in overtime|work=USA Today|access-date=October 23, 2011|date=February 26, 2011|archive-date=January 31, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131012102/https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-02-26-blazers-nuggets_N.htm|url-status=live}} The Blazers then faced the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the first round of the [[2011 NBA playoffs]]. Roy shot 1-for-8 the first 2 games, including a Game 2 where he saw only 8 minutes of playing time and went scoreless. The Blazers lost both games and trailed 2–0 in the series. He expressed his frustration about being the last substitution during the first 2 quarters, and playing for 8 minutes after getting 26 minutes in Game 1.{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-mavericks/headlines/20110420-turmoil-for-blazers-brandon-roy-complains-about-playing-time-vs.-mavericks.ece|author=SportsDayDFW.com|title=Turmoil for Blazers? Brandon Roy fights off tears, complains about playing time vs. Mavericks|publisher=SportsDayDFW.com|access-date=October 23, 2011|archive-date=August 18, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818095409/http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-mavericks/headlines/20110420-turmoil-for-blazers-brandon-roy-complains-about-playing-time-vs.-mavericks.ece|url-status=live}} Both the Blazers and Mavericks started Game 4 with a quiet first half, with Dallas leading slightly. The Blazers then missed their first 15 shots after halftime as the Mavs' lead grew as big as 67–44. Roy then made a three-pointer near the end of the third to cut the lead to 67–49. In the fourth quarter, Roy scored 18 points after going 1-for-3 the previous 3 quarters, including a clutch 4-point play to tie the game and a bank shot from the middle of the paint with 49 seconds left to give his team the lead for good, finishing with 24 points to lead the Blazers to an improbable 84–82 win to tie the series.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/columns/story?columnist=caplan_jeff&id=6417379|author=Jeff Caplan|title=Mavericks can't find answer for Roy|date=April 24, 2011|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 23, 2011|archive-date=August 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819111233/http://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/columns/story?columnist=caplan_jeff&id=6417379|url-status=live}} Just before NBA training camp opened following the resolution of the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Roy announced that his knees had degenerated so much—he lacked cartilage between the bones of both knees—that he was retiring from basketball. Following his announcement of retirement, the Portland Trail Blazers used their [[amnesty clause]] on Roy for [[NBA salary cap|salary cap]] flexibility.{{cite web | url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressRelease/tabid/297/itemid/2788/Default.aspx | title=Trail Blazers Designate Roy Contract for Amnesty | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc | date=December 15, 2011 | access-date=December 16, 2011 | url-status=usurped | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107234856/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressRelease/tabid/297/itemid/2788/Default.aspx | archive-date=January 7, 2012}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2012–2013)=== In June 2012, Roy announced that he was planning to make a comeback to the NBA. He said he had recovered enough to play after having the [[platelet-rich plasma]] procedure that [[Kobe Bryant]] also had to keep his knees healthy.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8219752/brandon-roy-minnesota-timberwolves-says-retirement-was-never-final-mind|title=Wolves introduce Brandon Roy|publisher=ESPN|date=July 31, 2012|access-date=July 31, 2012|archive-date=August 3, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120803005227/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/8219752/brandon-roy-minnesota-timberwolves-says-retirement-was-never-final-mind|url-status=live}}{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2011-jun-30-la-sp-kobe-bryant-knee-20110701-story.html|title=Kobe Bryant undergoes a different kind of knee procedure|date=June 30, 2011|access-date=July 31, 2012|work=Los Angeles Times|first1=Mike|last1=Bresnahan|first2=Broderick|last2=Turner|archive-date=October 14, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014014705/http://articles.latimes.com/2011/jun/30/sports/la-sp-kobe-bryant-knee-20110701|url-status=live}} He could not play for Portland under the current NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement because of Portland's amnesty of him in 2011. Roy entered the free agent market on July 1, 2012. Roy reportedly had expressed interest in signing with the Dallas Mavericks, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, Indiana Pacers, or Chicago Bulls.{{cite web|url=http://tracking.si.com/2012/07/01/brandon-roy-comeback-bulls-pacers-mavericks-warriors-timberwolves-injury-retire/|title=Report: Brandon Roy narrows free-agent list to five teams|date=July 1, 2012|access-date=July 31, 2012|work=SI.com|archive-date=August 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120806170830/http://tracking.si.com/2012/07/01/brandon-roy-comeback-bulls-pacers-mavericks-warriors-timberwolves-injury-retire/|url-status=live}} On July 31, 2012, Roy signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-3-time-nba-all-star-brandon-roy|title=Wolves Sign 3-Time NBA All-Star Brandon Roy|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=July 31, 2012|access-date=July 31, 2012|archive-date=August 1, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801172759/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-3-time-nba-all-star-brandon-roy|url-status=live}} The deal put Roy with All-Star forward [[Kevin Love]] and point guard [[Ricky Rubio]]. He decided to wear No. 3, the number he wore during his college years at Washington. He felt well during training camp but suffered an injury after a collision during a preseason game on October 26, 2012. He played in five regular season games before needing season-ending surgery on his right knee.{{cite web|title=Brandon Roy out at least a month|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8652156/brandon-roy-minnesota-timberwolves-least-month-yet-another-knee-surgery|publisher=ESPN|date=November 19, 2012|access-date=November 21, 2012|archive-date=November 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121120055047/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/8652156/brandon-roy-minnesota-timberwolves-least-month-yet-another-knee-surgery|url-status=live}} He averaged 5.8 points per game, 2.8 rebounds per game, and 4.6 assists per game in 24.4 minutes during the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]]. Roy was waived by Minnesota on May 10, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-waive-brandon-roy|title=Wolves Waive Brandon Roy|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=May 10, 2013|access-date=May 10, 2013|archive-date=May 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130518005147/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-waive-brandon-roy|url-status=live}} Afterwards, he said, "Any time you walk away from the game, you have 'what-ifs'. I feel like I was able to answer those questions last year by going out there and giving it a try."{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/60185/brandon-roy-calls-career|title=Brandon Roy calls it a career|work=ESPN|date=June 24, 2013|access-date=August 3, 2013|author=Kevin
